result.rationale: Verified: PollFeed imports RSS item content (`content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`), TopicEmbed.import passes it via PostCreator with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, and Post#cook now returns `raw` directly for raw_html posts, bypassing the normal cooking/sanitizer pipeline. Feed content rendered with `<%= raw post.cooked %>` in embed/best.html.erb executes for embed viewers. The mechanism is real and shown in the diff.

judged_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:22 — P1 confidence 100: `PostCreator.new(user, title: title, raw: absolutize_urls(url, contents), skip_validations: true, cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html])` stores attacker-controlled RSS `i.content` as unsanitized raw HTML, so a malicious or compromised configured feed persists scripts/event handlers that execute for every topic and embed viewer; although the configured feed URL is administrator-controlled, remote feed contents are outside the administrator's trust boundary and raw-html rendering removes the normal sanitizer.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies a security issue. In poll_feed.rb lines 31-34, RSS content is fetched and passed to TopicEmbed.import(). In topic_embed.rb line 22, PostCreator is called with cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]. In post.rb lines 131-133, when cook_method is raw_html, the raw content is returned directly without sanitization ('return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]'). This means malicious JavaScript in an RSS feed would be stored and rendered without sanitization. While the feed URL is admin-configured, the feed contents themselves come from an external source that could be compromised or malicious, creating a stored XSS vulnerability.
